identity.title: FlashSinkhorn: IO-Aware Entropic Optimal Transport on GPU

problem.claim: GPU solvers for entropic optimal transport via Sinkhorn iterations remain inefficient at scale.

gap.claim: Dense tensorized implementations incur quadratic HBM traffic, while existing online backends still depend on generic tiled map-reduce kernels with limited fusion.

contributions.claim: FlashSinkhorn rewrites stabilized log-domain Sinkhorn updates for squared Euclidean cost as row-wise LogSumExp reductions of biased dot-product scores, enabling attention-style fusion and tiling.
The solver uses fused Triton kernels that stream tiles through on-chip SRAM, update dual potentials in one pass, and retain linear-memory operations.
Streaming kernels are provided for transport application to support scalable first- and second-order optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present an IO-aware EOT solver that applies FlashAttention-style fusion and tiling to stabilized Sinkhorn updates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report up to 32× forward-pass and 161× end-to-end speedups over state-of-the-art online baselines on point-cloud OT on A100 GPUs.
The authors report improved scalability on OT-based downstream tasks.
The authors report releasing an open-source implementation for reproducibility.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper identifies poor scalability of GPU Sinkhorn solvers for entropic optimal transport.
It contrasts quadratic HBM traffic in dense tensorized methods with limited fusion in online backends.
FlashSinkhorn converts stabilized Sinkhorn updates into attention-like LogSumExp reductions and uses fused, SRAM-streaming Triton kernels.
Streaming transport-application kernels target scalable first- and second-order optimization.
The authors report large A100 speedups on point-cloud OT and improved downstream scalability, alongside an open-source release.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects an algebraic reformulation of Sinkhorn updates to a known hardware-efficient attention pattern, then ties that reformulation to reduced HBM IO.

lessons.interpretation: A precise equivalence can make an optimization idea legible while exposing reusable systems primitives.
lessons.application: When proposing a hardware-aware algorithm, explicitly identify the computational pattern it reduces to and state which memory movement or fusion bottleneck that mapping addresses.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the reformulation changes numerical behavior materially or lacks a compatible fused kernel.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark sizes, baseline identities, speedup measurement conditions, or statistical variability.
The downstream tasks and the meaning of improved scalability are not described.
Numerical accuracy, convergence behavior, hardware utilization, and implementation details are not reported in the abstract.
